reason: Verified in source and by driving the page. render-b.js states["owner-editing"].move() writes only two things: item.querySelector('.b-away').textContent and read.textContent = "in " + current + " days". Nothing else derived from the date is touched. Driven at 1440 on ?v=approach&state=owner-editing: before the press the row reads away 23, .b-date "Sat 8 Aug" (uppercased by b.css:199, so the frame's "SAT 8 AUG" is accurate), .b-grab aria-label "Send the invitations, Saturday 8 August, in 23 days. Shown to guests. Open to change it.", readout "Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 days". After one press of "Move a week earlier": away 16, top 322px to 224px, .b-date STILL "Sat 8 Aug", .b-grab aria-label STILL "…Saturday 8 August, in 23 days…", readout collapses to "in 16 days". After a further +1 the same two fields remain frozen at 8 August. So the item's only spelled-out date goes stale on the first press and the readout stops naming a date at all, in the one gesture this direction is built around. The gate does not cover it: interaction-check.mjs:310 asserts only readout.includes(String(moved.away)). Not taste, not already handled, no constraint touched (no colour, weight, family or architecture change). Confirmed. The fix is directionally right but imprecise in three ways and would introduce a new defect as written, so it is sharpened below.
sharpenedFix: In render-b.js states["owner-editing"], make the date the single source and rewrite every fact from it in the same frame, but fix the fix: (1) Do NOT hardcode Date.UTC(2026,6,16). TODAY lives in fixture.js:17 and is exposed as F.today; derive the base from it: var base = Date.UTC.apply(null, F.today.split('-').map(Number).map(function(n,i){return i===1?n-1:n;})), then var iso = new Date(base + current*86400000).toISOString().slice(0,10). A literal epoch in render-b.js silently rots the moment the fixture's review date moves. (2) The proposed aria-label template interpolates a `visibility` variable that does not exist in that scope, and drops the existing sentence. Write the exact string the measure() builder already writes so a moved row and an untouched row read identically: title + ', ' + F.fmt.long(iso) + ', in ' + current + ' days. Shown to guests. Open to change it.' Keep .b-away a bare number (the existing comment about the column's one grammar is right) and set .b-date to F.fmt.weekdayShort(iso) + ' ' + F.fmt.short(iso). (3) THE REAL RISK the finding misses: keeping the full date in .b-stepRead at every value reflows the stepper under the pointer. Measured at 1440 today, the first press already collapses .b-stepRow from two lines to one and throws "Move a day later" from x=751,y=819 to x=960,y=783 — over 200px out from under the cursor, so a second press lands on nothing. Restoring the date does not fix that: the readout swings 327px ("Sunday 2 August 2026 · in 17 days") to 356px ("Saturday 15 August 2026 · in 30 days") to 396px (two-line wrap) as weekday and month names change length, still sliding the buttons ~50px sideways per press. So pair the date restoration with a stable slot: in b.css give .b-stepRead a fixed measure (min-width sized to the longest in-range string, ~26ch, text-align:center, white-space:nowrap) or lift it onto its own line above the four buttons, so the four .b-step boxes never move between presses. (4) Give the readout role="status" — it is the only thing that announces the change, and nothing in the editor is a live region today (the only role="status" in render-b.js is the undo bar at line 214). (5) Gate it in interaction-check.mjs: after one -7 and one +1, assert the count, the .b-date line, the .b-grab accessible name and the .b-stepRead all name the same single date, AND assert the four .b-step bounding boxes are byte-identical before and after both presses.
